cards.front: Recall a key point about Hardware & Software
cards.back: Hardware refers to the physical components of a computer system - the parts you can see and touch. Hardware includes all the electronic and mechanical parts that make up the computer.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hardware & Software
cards.back: Software refers to the programs, instructions, and data that tell the hardware what to do. Software is not physical - it is the set of instructions that the hardware executes.

cards.front: What should you know about key concept?
cards.back: Hardware and software are interdependent. Hardware needs software to give it instructions; software needs hardware to execute those instructions. Neither can function without the other.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hardware & Software
cards.back: System software manages and controls the hardware and provides a platform for application software to run on. It runs in the background and the user may not directly interact with it.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Hardware & Software
cards.back: Application software performs specific tasks for the user. It sits on top of the system software and is what the user directly interacts with.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse computer science exam tips?
cards.back: Hardware = physical, Software = programs. System software vs Application software — learn examples of each. RAM: volatile, read-write, working storage. ROM: non-volatile, read-only, boot instructions. When comparing components, use a table format. For performance questions, consider ALL relevant components, not just the CPU. Always explain WHY a component is needed, not just what it does.
